When adding Presence via Growth, Green may use destroyed disks instead of track disks even while disks remain on tracks: this is free while Healthy, or costs 1 Energy per destroyed disk while Blighted. This permission applies only to Growth; an ordinary Power needs its own explicit destroyed-Presence permission. Green's separate **Always** Range-2 Jungle/Wetland placement is additional to its one chosen Growth group, including when it chooses Reclaim/gain a Power. It still chooses only one of the optional groups. Growth instructions from multiple options can be ordered together, so a gained Power may inform the mandatory placement. Its explicit regeneration can use destroyed Presence; ordinary placement cannot. [Core: .9v5kc2v, .7w4g8r1, .bu6oegz, .7w4g8nv]
- **Thunderspeaker:** Presence may accompany each moved Dahan, including generic Move as well as Gather/Push; two Dahan can carry two Presence. **Sworn to Victory** triggers after an entire single-land Ravage for each Dahan destroyed there: destroy one of Thunderspeaker's Presence within Range 1 per Dahan, even if no Blight was added. Finish the Ravage, cascades and counterattack before this triggered loss. [Core: .bu6oc6l, .bu6oc73, .bu6ofsi]
- **Ocean's Hungry Grasp:** On a board with any of Ocean's Presence, the Ocean is a Coastal Wetland for **Powers and Blight**, not for normal Growth, Invader actions or Fear Cards. Powers and Special Rules can measure Range through it as a land. [Core: range-through-ocean] Powers can target it and move Invaders/Dahan into it; Blight can cascade into it. Other Spirits' Presence may end up there via a legal Power, including Thunderspeaker accompanying moved Dahan. You can measure Growth placement Range **from existing Ocean Presence**, although normal Growth cannot add to the Ocean just by treating it as a Coastal Wetland. The Growth group explicitly adding two Presence in **any Ocean** can place them in any board's Ocean, even a board where Ocean has no Presence, without a numeric Range requirement. Its other group's Range-1 **Coastal land** placement does not permit placing in the Ocean. Other placement must respect Ocean's land-type restriction unless expressly ignored (e.g., **Indomitable Claim** for Inland Presence). [Core: .bu6odcf, .7w4gef8, .9v5kf36, .9v5ka9o, .9v5kc4i, When-OHG-is-in-play-can-other-pieces-end-up-in-the-Ocean]
- **Drowning:** Ocean's rule Drowns Invaders/Dahan **after** they move into the Ocean on a board with Ocean's Presence; Ocean need not have a disk in the Ocean itself. Drown destroys: Town/City Fear happens immediately, and drowned Invaders go on Ocean's panel. At any time, trade stored Invaders: **X printed Health worth of drowned Invaders for 1 Energy**, X = number of Spirits; ignore Health modifiers and make change. They need not be exchanged when Drowned; Ocean may exchange them between actions during a later Spirit Phase, including before paying for cards. Dahan drowning gives no Energy. Ordinary destruction, including thematically watery Powers, is not Drowning unless specified. If Ocean loses all Presence on that board mid-action, Ocean In Play lasts through the action tree; afterward non-human pieces left there remain physically but out of play until it returns. Humans cannot stay there between action trees: if Drowning fails, Push survivors to non-Ocean lands within that action. This is an actual Push and can trigger applicable movement effects, unlike later cleanup. Failed Drowning yields no Energy. Remaining illegal humans are cleaned up to the nearest legal land afterward. Cleanup is not an action, move, removal or destruction and triggers nothing, and occurs before the outcome check. If no legal land exists return humans to supply as cleanup. [Core: .7w4g8qy, .9v5kbka, .7w4g8pb, .9v5ka9g, .7w4g8r4, .9v5kfqb, .9v5kfqs, .7w4gdtl]
- **Bringer of Dreams and Nightmares:** Its Powers' explicit Damage/Destroy cannot actually harm Invaders/Dahan or destroy anything except its own Presence. An explicit instruction to Damage or Destroy Dahan does nothing to those Dahan; skip that instruction and resolve the rest of the Power normally. For each Power use, evaluate what it would destroy if resolved normally: generate **0 Fear per Explorer, 2 per Town, 5 per City**, and Push the would-be-destroyed Explorers/Towns. No real Damage is marked, so different Powers or a Repeat cannot combine their hypothetical Damage; multiple instructions **within one Power** can. Existing real Damage from others helps its hypothetical destruction and remains unchanged afterward. Within a single Power use, a given Invader can be pretend-destroyed only once. Repeats can “destroy” the same piece again for Fear. It does not get bonuses conditional on **actual** destruction (e.g., Mists of Oblivion or Vengeance of the Dead) from these pretend destructions. [Core: .7w4g7yx, .7w4g7yu, .7w4g8pj, .9v5kfh3, .9v5katc, .bu6oc6g]
- **Bringer's exceptions:** Fear Cards and Dahan counterattacks after its Defend deal real Damage, because they are not its Power's Damage. Bringer can Remove/Replace, add real Blight (destroying Presence normally), modify Invader actions or cause actual Ravage. Reducing Health or replacing a damaged piece with a lower-Health one can cause real destruction by core Health rules. If Bringer Pushes a “destroyed” Town into Ocean, Ocean's separate Drowning destroys it: **3 total Fear** (2 from Bringer, 1 from Ocean). **Spirits May Yet Dream** can flip any Fear Card, earned or anywhere in the deck. Its Element-granting level gives the target Spirit one Element of a type it already has at least one of; it cannot grant a currently absent Element type. [Core: .9v5ka92, .7w4g9jv, .9v5kf34, can-bringer-destroy-things-indirectly, .7w4g8pf, .7w4g8rd]
- **Call on Midnight's Dream:** “Forget this Power” refers to that card, not the newly gained card. Forgetting it to satisfy the gained Major's ordinary Forget requirement also satisfies its conditional; no second Forget is required. The forgotten card leaves play and cannot later be repeated via the normal once-this-turn permission. [Core: .9v5kc3z, .7w4gani, .9v5ka8w]

requested_parts: Bringer uses a Power whose explicit instructions include Damage or Destroy Dahan, followed by other legal effects. Are the Dahan harmed, and must the entire Power be skipped?
answers.answer: Bringer ignores explicit Dahan Damage/Destroy instruction; skip it and resolve rest normally.

- The **targeting Range box** gives the maximum land distance from **one of your Presence**. Range 0 requires your Presence in the target land. Origin icons may require your Sacred Site or Presence in a particular terrain.
- Target restrictions may specify terrain, Coastal/Inland, contents, or a Spirit. A slash between piece/terrain icons means either or both types, not an additional allowance for each.
- Unless explicitly different, use **one target land or Spirit, once per turn**. Multiple effects and all innate levels apply to that same target. You cannot pay twice for an ordinary card use or use an innate twice just by having twice its Elements.
- Resolve instructions in printed order, doing as much as possible. Inability to perform one instruction does not prohibit playing or using a Power on an otherwise legal target. Target restrictions are in its target bar, not implied by its text. You may even target a land where the effects accomplish nothing, but must actually attempt the text to count as using/targeting the Power.
- You may forego the whole Power, but cannot arbitrarily omit a possible mandatory instruction after starting. “Up to” allows zero. “Or” chooses between its adjoining clauses, not other separate text on the card. Choose the branch **before resolving either option**; you cannot start one to inspect its results and then switch to the other. [FAQ .9v5kcmx]
- Resolve the base effect and every met threshold in printed order **unless explicit timing text says otherwise**: “First” and “Before” can place a threshold instruction ahead of earlier-printed base instructions. A level saying **Instead** replaces previous effects rather than adding to them. You may treat yourself as having fewer Elements **for the whole Power**, consistently, rather than selecting individual thresholds to omit.
- Check Elements when a threshold is reached: newly gained Elements can enable later levels; losing Elements can prevent later levels, without changing completed effects. Apply a threshold changing Speed, Range or targeting when checking that attribute, before the ordinary effects: for example, Thunderspeaker's met Fast threshold permits using its Innate in Fast. Speed/Range/targeting modifiers are checked in time to use them before targeting, and an “or” choice is made before its branch resolves.
- Non-board-changing effects last for this turn only unless explicitly stated otherwise. Defend and action skips do not remain for future turns.

- **Initial Blight:** Exactly one extra Blight total at setup, with or without a card; never repeat this on flips. This and outcome timing above are substantive corrections to older rulebook wording. [Setup: one-more-blight-errata]

They do **not** increase the amount of another Range bonus: another boost cannot turn **Reaching Grasp**'s printed +2 into a larger bonus. They do not extend another Spirit's Powers merely because those Powers target the boosted Spirit. A bonus restricted to Powers does not extend Growth; Power Cards also resolve after normal Growth has finished. requested_parts: A Power's own threshold gives it +1 Range. If the threshold is met on both the original use and its Repeat, does the Repeat get +2 Range?
If that threshold is no longer met on the Repeat, is the first +1 retained?
answers.answer: No stack same Range bonus; +1 persists on Repeat even if threshold no longer met.

requested_parts: A Spirit plays two Power Cards and later Repeats one. For an effect counting Power Cards played, such as Boon of Vigor, is the count two or three?
Does the Repeat consume another ordinary Card Play, and does it nevertheless count as a new Power use?
answers.answer: Count 2 card plays, not 3; Repeat no Card Play but is another Power use.

evidence.text: A Repeat activates a Power's effects again; it is not a second card play and grants no additional printed card Elements. It **does** count as another Power use. For effects counting cards played (such as Boon of Vigor), a Repeat adds no card play; count the card's original play only. A repeated effect explicitly granting Elements grants those again. Recheck thresholds using your current Elements; they were not spent on the original, but may since have been lost.

Retain changes to the Power, including extra Range or changed speed. An ordinary Repeat uses the Power's **most recently assigned speed**: a Slow Power repeats in Slow even if its permission came from a Fast Power; a formerly Fast Power explicitly made Slow before repeating now repeats in Slow. An instruction to Repeat immediately instead follows that explicit timing, directly after the originating use. [FAQ repeating-powers-with-changed-speeds] You may postpone choosing which eligible card to repeat until you actually repeat it, and make different choices/targets then. For **Powerstorm** and **Gift of Strength**, the Spirit receives a once-this-turn option rather than a grant-time selection of cards: a card played later that turn may be selected while it remains in play, subject to the permission’s restrictions and cost. [FAQ timing-of-choosing-powers-for-once-this-turn-repeats] Gift of Strength imposes its printed card-cost eligibility ceiling but requires no additional Energy payment for the Repeat, so an eligible card may be repeated with no Energy left. If the permission requires paying a cost, pay it as instructed. **Powerstorm** requires paying the repeated Power Card's Energy cost again when exercising each Repeat, including its threshold's further permissions; the original play payment does not cover it.

- **Range boosts:** Numeric Range boosts do not waive source/target restrictions or the requirement “one of your lands.” A Power still requiring your Sacred Site must have such an origin. General Power Range boosts affect Range values with a **printed Range arrow** in Powers **used by the Spirit receiving the bonus**, including effect-text arrows, subject to all restrictions. They do **not** increase the amount of another Range bonus: another boost cannot turn **Reaching Grasp**'s printed +2 into a larger bonus. They do not extend another Spirit's Powers merely because those Powers target the boosted Spirit. A bonus restricted to Powers does not extend Growth; Power Cards also resolve after normal Growth has finished. A special rule granting extra Range specifically for targeting lands with certain contents changes only the targeting Range box: **Shadows of the Dahan** does not extend effect-text Range arrows. In a Spirit-targeting Power's effects, measure from the Presence of the Spirit following that instruction (usually the target Spirit), unless the Power says otherwise. requested_parts: A Blighted Island instruction simply tells each Spirit to destroy one of its Presence. May a Spirit choose a disk still covering its Presence track to uncover a benefit instead of destroying island Presence, and where does a destroyed disk go?
answers.answer: No, Presence actions affect island Presence, not track disks. Destroyed disks beside island, not back on track.

requested_parts: In standard setup using a Blight Card, how is the card chosen, which side starts face-up, and may players inspect its reverse before choosing or starting?
answers.answer: Randomly select Blight Card, Healthy side up; don't inspect reverse.

answers.answer: Yes, Innate available each turn if Elements met; ordinarily no Energy or Card Play cost.

requested_parts: Without an effect granting a Repeat or another use, may a Spirit pay a Power Card's printed Energy cost twice to use it twice in one turn?

answers.answer: No, cannot pay twice absent Repeat/permission. Made Fast is Fast only, not also Slow.

requested_parts: For a standard game, how many balanced Island Boards are used and chosen, how are their initial Invaders, Dahan and Blight placed, and how are the Minor/Major decks and shared piece supplies prepared?
answers.answer: One random board per Spirit; balanced layout per player count. Populate all lands per printed icons. Shuffle Minor/Major decks separately with own discards; make Invader/Dahan/Energy supplies available; standard Invader deck stage prep separately.

For two, any fitting arrangement is legal; the rulebook illustrates bottom-to-bottom with Oceans facing opposite outer corners. For three use the triangular layout, and for four the two-row parallelogram layout illustrated in CORE pp.6–7. [FAQ .7w4g8pg] Populate every land with its printed Invader, Dahan and Blight setup icons. Setup Blight comes from the box, never the Blight pool, and does not cascade or destroy Presence.
2. **Invader deck:** Shuffle each stage separately. Remove one card of each stage unseen. Stack **3 Stage I cards on top, 4 Stage II below them, 5 Stage III at the bottom**. Put this 12-card deck in Explore.
3. **Fear:** Put **4 Fear markers per Spirit** in the Fear Pool. Shuffle the 15 Fear Cards and use 9 unseen: three cards, Terror II divider, three cards, Terror III divider, three cards, from top to bottom. Start at Terror I. Leave space for Earned Fear Cards and Fear discard.
4. **Blight:** Randomly select a Blight Card, Healthy Island side up; do not inspect its reverse. Put **2 Blight per Spirit plus exactly 1 additional Blight total** on it. 5. **Supply:** Shuffle Minor and Major decks separately, each with its own discard. Make Invaders, Dahan and Energy available to everyone.

requested_parts: Ocean In Play is active on a board. Infinite Vitality with its threshold protects Dahan in that Ocean, and a Power Pushes a Dahan into it. Ocean In Play triggers but cannot destroy that Dahan. With an adjacent non-Ocean land available, what happens next: does the Dahan remain until cleanup, or is it Pushed?
Is that relocation an actual Push within the triggered action or merely cleanup?
answers.answer: Dahan protected means Drowning fails; if legal adjacent land, Ocean Pushes survivor there during triggered action. Actual Push, not cleanup.

requested_parts: A land-targeting Power Card is Repeated using a permission that does not specify where the Repeat occurs. Must it use the original target land?
May it instead use another legal land, and do the ordinary Range and Target restrictions still apply?
answers.answer: No specified Repeat target means any normally legal target, including original; ordinary Range/target rules apply.

requested_parts: Concealing Shadows has already resolved in Fast, so Dahan in its target land take no Damage from Ravaging Invaders this turn. That land now Ravages with one Town, one Explorer and two healthy Dahan, no Defend and no prior Blight. What happens to land and Dahan, how much counterattack Damage is available, and can it destroy both Invaders for how much Ravage-generated Fear?
answers.answer: Land takes 3 Damage -> one Blight. Concealing protects Dahan from Invader Ravage Damage, so zero Dahan Damage; both Dahan survive and deal 4 counterattack. They can destroy Town (2 damage) and Explorer (1) for 1 Fear from Town.

1. **Island:** Randomly choose one Island Board per Spirit and join the balanced sides into the island. For one Spirit use one board. For two, any fitting arrangement is legal; the rulebook illustrates bottom-to-bottom with Oceans facing opposite outer corners. For three use the triangular layout, and for four the two-row parallelogram layout illustrated in CORE pp.6–7. [FAQ .7w4g8pg] Populate every land with its printed Invader, Dahan and Blight setup icons. Setup Blight comes from the box, never the Blight pool, and does not cascade or destroy Presence.
2. **Invader deck:** Shuffle each stage separately. Remove one card of each stage unseen. Stack **3 Stage I cards on top, 4 Stage II below them, 5 Stage III at the bottom**. Put this 12-card deck in Explore.
3. **Fear:** Put **4 Fear markers per Spirit** in the Fear Pool. Shuffle the 15 Fear Cards and use 9 unseen: three cards, Terror II divider, three cards, Terror III divider, three cards, from top to bottom. Start at Terror I. Leave space for Earned Fear Cards and Fear discard.
4. **Blight:** Randomly select a Blight Card, Healthy Island side up; do not inspect its reverse. Put **2 Blight per Spirit plus exactly 1 additional Blight total** on it. This is the official initial-pool correction. The additional 1 is applied only at setup, never again on a card flip. Remaining box Blight is separate from this pool.
5. **Supply:** Shuffle Minor and Major decks separately, each with its own discard. Make Invaders, Dahan and Energy available to everyone.
6. **Spirits:** Each player takes one color's 13 Presence and reminder markers (any accidental extra disk is a spare, not additional Presence for play), a different Spirit panel, and that Spirit's four Unique cards as their starting hand. Each starts on a different Island Board and follows the back-of-panel setup exactly. Where several choices equally satisfy setup, choose freely; separate Presence-placement instructions may use the same land. Put remaining disks on the dashed spaces of both Presence tracks; the leftmost solid starting spaces remain uncovered. Starting boards do not restrict where a Spirit can act after setup.
7. **Initial Explore:** Reveal the top Invader card and Explore normally. Then put it face-up in **Build**. This Explore is the last part of setup; Ravage starts empty. The first actual turn begins with the Spirit Phase.

**Defend N** reduces each occurrence of Invader Damage to both land and Dahan by N for this turn, to a minimum of zero. Multiple Defend effects add. It does not reduce Spirit Damage or make Dahan do less counterattack Damage. Land and Dahan receive the reduction separately, not by splitting a shared allowance. A protection explicitly limited to Dahan is different: **Concealing Shadows** makes Dahan take no Damage from Ravaging Invaders this turn, while land still takes its normal Damage and can Blight. Protected surviving Dahan then counterattack normally. It does not protect them from direct Destroy instructions or Damage from other sources. [FAQ .7w4g8nu; original card text]

requested_parts: An effect explicitly adds two Blight simultaneously to one land containing two Presence from each of two Spirits. Counting only Presence destroyed in that land by this one addition, how many disks does each Spirit lose?
Would adding one Blight there in each of two separate completed instructions destroy Presence once or twice, assuming each Spirit still has Presence there?
answers.answer: One Presence from each Spirit for a single Blight addition regardless two Blight tokens (one per Spirit, so each loses 1). Two separate additions each destroy one per Spirit, so 2 each if remain.

3. **Fear:** Put **4 Fear markers per Spirit** in the Fear Pool. Shuffle the 15 Fear Cards and use 9 unseen: three cards, Terror II divider, three cards, Terror III divider, three cards, from top to bottom. Start at Terror I. Leave space for Earned Fear Cards and Fear discard.
4. **Blight:** Randomly select a Blight Card, Healthy Island side up; do not inspect its reverse. Put **2 Blight per Spirit plus exactly 1 additional Blight total** on it. This is the official initial-pool correction. The additional 1 is applied only at setup, never again on a card flip. Remaining box Blight is separate from this pool.
5. **Supply:** Shuffle Minor and Major decks separately, each with its own discard. Make Invaders, Dahan and Energy available to everyone.

Each starts on a different Island Board and follows the back-of-panel setup exactly. Where several choices equally satisfy setup, choose freely; separate Presence-placement instructions may use the same land. requested_parts: Concealing Shadows has resolved on a land. Later that turn, Poisoned Land resolves there and instructs the Spirit to destroy all Dahan. Does Concealing Shadows prevent those destructions?
If Infinite Vitality's threshold had also resolved on that land this turn, would that threshold prevent them?
answers.answer: Concealing only protects Dahan from Ravaging Invaders, not direct destroy. Infinite Vitality prevents Destroy, so would save them.

evidence.text: **Defend N** reduces each occurrence of Invader Damage to both land and Dahan by N for this turn, to a minimum of zero. Multiple Defend effects add. It does not reduce Spirit Damage or make Dahan do less counterattack Damage. Land and Dahan receive the reduction separately, not by splitting a shared allowance. A protection explicitly limited to Dahan is different: **Concealing Shadows** makes Dahan take no Damage from Ravaging Invaders this turn, while land still takes its normal Damage and can Blight. requested_parts: A Spirit Power directly and explicitly deals 2 Damage to Dahan
it does not cause a Ravage. Would Defend 3 reduce this Damage?
Would Concealing Shadows prevent it?
Would Infinite Vitality’s threshold prevent it?
Separately, if Invaders Ravage for 2 Damage in a land with Defend 3, how much reaches the land and Dahan?
answers.answer: Defend and Concealing don't stop direct Spirit Damage to Dahan; Infinite Vitality threshold prevents Dahan damage/destroy. Ravage 2 with Defend 3 leaves zero to land and Dahan.

requested_parts: Spirit A has an existing +2 bonus to its Power Ranges and uses Reaching Grasp, whose text grants target Spirit B +2 Range with all their Powers. Does A’s existing bonus increase the amount granted to +4, or does B receive +2?
Does B’s Power-only bonus cover Innate Powers as well as Power Cards, and can it extend ordinary Growth placement?
answers.answer: A's +2 doesn't boost Reaching Grasp's fixed +2 grant; B receives +2. Applies B's all Powers including Innates, not Growth.

requested_parts: For a Range arrow within a Power’s effect text, where is the origin for a land-targeting Power?
Where is it for a Spirit-targeting Power used by Spirit A that instructs Spirit B to act?
Which Spirit’s Range bonuses apply, and if that internal arrow is Range 1 with A having +2 and B having no bonus, what Range can it reach from whose Presence?
How does Blazing Renewal’s explicit measurement origin differ?
answers.answer: Internal arrow land-targeting from target land; Spirit-targeting from Spirit whose instruction is followed (usually target Spirit). A's bonuses apply even with B origin. With Range 1 +2 A, reach 3 from B's Presence. Blazing Renewal explicitly uses user's Presence.

evidence.text:
- The **targeting Range box** gives the maximum land distance from **one of your Presence**. Range 0 requires your Presence in the target land. Origin icons may require your Sacred Site or Presence in a particular terrain.
- Target restrictions may specify terrain, Coastal/Inland, contents, or a Spirit. A slash between piece/terrain icons means either or both types, not an additional allowance for each.
- Unless explicitly different, use **one target land or Spirit, once per turn**. Multiple effects and all innate levels apply to that same target. You cannot pay twice for an ordinary card use or use an innate twice just by having twice its Elements.
- Resolve instructions in printed order, doing as much as possible. Inability to perform one instruction does not prohibit playing or using a Power on an otherwise legal target. Target restrictions are in its target bar, not implied by its text. You may even target a land where the effects accomplish nothing, but must actually attempt the text to count as using/targeting the Power.
- You may forego the whole Power, but cannot arbitrarily omit a possible mandatory instruction after starting. “Up to” allows zero. “Or” chooses between its adjoining clauses, not other separate text on the card. Choose the branch **before resolving either option**; you cannot start one to inspect its results and then switch to the other. [FAQ .9v5kcmx]
- Resolve the base effect and every met threshold in printed order **unless explicit timing text says otherwise**: “First” and “Before” can place a threshold instruction ahead of earlier-printed base instructions. A level saying **Instead** replaces previous effects rather than adding to them. You may treat yourself as having fewer Elements **for the whole Power**, consistently, rather than selecting individual thresholds to omit.
- Check Elements when a threshold is reached: newly gained Elements can enable later levels; losing Elements can prevent later levels, without changing completed effects. Apply a threshold changing Speed, Range or targeting when checking that attribute, before the ordinary effects: for example, Thunderspeaker's met Fast threshold permits using its Innate in Fast. Speed/Range/targeting modifiers are checked in time to use them before targeting, and an “or” choice is made before its branch resolves.

requested_parts: A Spirit plays and pays for a Power Card, then foregoes its entire text because it has no legal target or the Spirit chooses not to use it. With no other effect removing the card, do its printed Elements remain available for Innates, is its Energy refunded, and does the card leave play immediately or during Time Passes?
answers.answer: Elements remain; no refund; card stays in play until Time Passes/discard.

3. **Fear:** Put **4 Fear markers per Spirit** in the Fear Pool. Shuffle the 15 Fear Cards and use 9 unseen: three cards, Terror II divider, three cards, Terror III divider, three cards, from top to bottom. Start at Terror I. Leave space for Earned Fear Cards and Fear discard.
4. **Blight:** Randomly select a Blight Card, Healthy Island side up; do not inspect its reverse. Put **2 Blight per Spirit plus exactly 1 additional Blight total** on it. requested_parts: Two separate Ravages occur in the same land before Time Passes. Each would deal 4 Damage before the land’s Defend 3
assume that pre-Defend total stays 4, and one Dahan starts healthy. Is Defend expended on the first Ravage?
How much Damage reaches land and Dahan each time?
Do the two 1-Damage land results combine into Blight, and what happens to that Dahan on the second Ravage?
answers.answer: Defend not expended, applies each separate Ravage. Each gets 1 damage to land and Dahan. One land Damage doesn't accumulate/save to later action, so no Blight. Healthy Dahan takes 1 in first Ravage, second 1 kills it.

evidence.text:
1. **Island:** Randomly choose one Island Board per Spirit and join the balanced sides into the island. For one Spirit use one board. For two, any fitting arrangement is legal; the rulebook illustrates bottom-to-bottom with Oceans facing opposite outer corners. For three use the triangular layout, and for four the two-row parallelogram layout illustrated in CORE pp.6–7. [FAQ .7w4g8pg] Populate every land with its printed Invader, Dahan and Blight setup icons. Setup Blight comes from the box, never the Blight pool, and does not cascade or destroy Presence.
2. **Invader deck:** Shuffle each stage separately. Remove one card of each stage unseen. Stack **3 Stage I cards on top, 4 Stage II below them, 5 Stage III at the bottom**. Put this 12-card deck in Explore.
3. **Fear:** Put **4 Fear markers per Spirit** in the Fear Pool. Shuffle the 15 Fear Cards and use 9 unseen: three cards, Terror II divider, three cards, Terror III divider, three cards, from top to bottom. Start at Terror I. Leave space for Earned Fear Cards and Fear discard.
4. **Blight:** Randomly select a Blight Card, Healthy Island side up; do not inspect its reverse. Put **2 Blight per Spirit plus exactly 1 additional Blight total** on it. This is the official initial-pool correction. The additional 1 is applied only at setup, never again on a card flip. Remaining box Blight is separate from this pool.
5. **Supply:** Shuffle Minor and Major decks separately, each with its own discard. Make Invaders, Dahan and Energy available to everyone.
6. **Spirits:** Each player takes one color's 13 Presence and reminder markers (any accidental extra disk is a spare, not additional Presence for play), a different Spirit panel, and that Spirit's four Unique cards as their starting hand. Each starts on a different Island Board and follows the back-of-panel setup exactly. Where several choices equally satisfy setup, choose freely; separate Presence-placement instructions may use the same land. Put remaining disks on the dashed spaces of both Presence tracks; the leftmost solid starting spaces remain uncovered. Starting boards do not restrict where a Spirit can act after setup.
7. **Initial Explore:** Reveal the top Invader card and Explore normally. Then put it face-up in **Build**. This Explore is the last part of setup; Ravage starts empty. The first actual turn begins with the Spirit Phase.

- The **targeting Range box** gives the maximum land distance from **one of your Presence**. Range 0 requires your Presence in the target land. Origin icons may require your Sacred Site or Presence in a particular terrain.

- Unless explicitly different, use **one target land or Spirit, once per turn**. Multiple effects and all innate levels apply to that same target. You cannot pay twice for an ordinary card use or use an innate twice just by having twice its Elements.
- Resolve instructions in printed order, doing as much as possible. Inability to perform one instruction does not prohibit playing or using a Power on an otherwise legal target. Target restrictions are in its target bar, not implied by its text. You may even target a land where the effects accomplish nothing, but must actually attempt the text to count as using/targeting the Power.

requested_parts: A Power has a lower threshold requiring 2 Water and a higher threshold requiring 3 Water. Its Spirit has 3 Water. May the Spirit resolve that Power as if it had only 2 Water, getting the lower threshold but not the higher one?
May another Power still check the Spirit's actual 3 Water later this turn?
Assume no instruction gains or loses Elements.
answers.answer: Yes, choose fewer Elements for whole Power consistently, resolve lower threshold not higher; later Power sees actual 3 Water.

[Core: .9v5ka92, .7w4g9jv, .9v5kf34, can-bringer-destroy-things-indirectly, .7w4g8pf, .7w4g8rd]

requested_parts: A Spirit has several separate Growth options and no instruction allowing more than one choice. During one Spirit Phase, may it combine the Energy action from one option with the Add Presence action from a different option, or must it choose a single entire option?
answers.answer: Must choose one whole Growth option.

- Target restrictions may specify terrain, Coastal/Inland, contents, or a Spirit. A slash between piece/terrain icons means either or both types, not an additional allowance for each.
- Unless explicitly different, use **one target land or Spirit, once per turn**. Multiple effects and all innate levels apply to that same target. You cannot pay twice for an ordinary card use or use an innate twice just by having twice its Elements.
- Resolve instructions in printed order, doing as much as possible. Inability to perform one instruction does not prohibit playing or using a Power on an otherwise legal target. Target restrictions are in its target bar, not implied by its text. You may even target a land where the effects accomplish nothing, but must actually attempt the text to count as using/targeting the Power.
- You may forego the whole Power, but cannot arbitrarily omit a possible mandatory instruction after starting. “Up to” allows zero. “Or” chooses between its adjoining clauses, not other separate text on the card. Choose the branch **before resolving either option**; you cannot start one to inspect its results and then switch to the other. [FAQ .9v5kcmx]

A level saying **Instead** replaces previous effects rather than adding to them. requested_parts: An ordinary land-targeting Power has printed Range 1, Target ANY and no special origin requirement. Your Presence is in land A, and land B is adjacent to A. Assuming all other restrictions are met, may you target A as well as B, or must the target be exactly one land away from your Presence?
answers.answer: Range 1 is maximum; may target A at Range 0 or B at 1.

evidence.text:

Target restrictions are in its target bar, not implied by its text. You may even target a land where the effects accomplish nothing, but must actually attempt the text to count as using/targeting the Power.

requested_parts: In a standard core game a land is already crowded with Invaders, Dahan, and Spirit Presence. Can a general per-land stacking limit prevent an otherwise legal Build, Gather, or Presence placement there?
Do any of those three types of piece have such a default cap?
answers.answer: No stacking limit; Invaders, Dahan not limited by supplied pieces; Presence limited by disks only (crowding isn't cap).

evidence.text: Invaders and Dahan are not limited by the supplied pieces; use substitutes or Energy markers to mark multiples if necessary. No standard stacking limit applies to pieces in a land. Presence is limited to your disks; destroyed disks are separate from unused track disks. [CORE pp.13,15–16; FAQ .9v5ka9f]

1. **Island:** Randomly choose one Island Board per Spirit and join the balanced sides into the island. For one Spirit use one board. For two, any fitting arrangement is legal; the rulebook illustrates bottom-to-bottom with Oceans facing opposite outer corners. For three use the triangular layout, and for four the two-row parallelogram layout illustrated in CORE pp.6–7. [FAQ .7w4g8pg] Populate every land with its printed Invader, Dahan and Blight setup icons. Setup Blight comes from the box, never the Blight pool, and does not cascade or destroy Presence.
2. **Invader deck:** Shuffle each stage separately. Remove one card of each stage unseen. Stack **3 Stage I cards on top, 4 Stage II below them, 5 Stage III at the bottom**. Put this 12-card deck in Explore.
3. **Fear:** Put **4 Fear markers per Spirit** in the Fear Pool. Shuffle the 15 Fear Cards and use 9 unseen: three cards, Terror II divider, three cards, Terror III divider, three cards, from top to bottom. Start at Terror I. Leave space for Earned Fear Cards and Fear discard.
4. **Blight:** Randomly select a Blight Card, Healthy Island side up; do not inspect its reverse. Put **2 Blight per Spirit plus exactly 1 additional Blight total** on it. This is the official initial-pool correction. The additional 1 is applied only at setup, never again on a card flip. Remaining box Blight is separate from this pool.
5. **Supply:** Shuffle Minor and Major decks separately, each with its own discard. Make Invaders, Dahan and Energy available to everyone.
6. **Spirits:** Each player takes one color's 13 Presence and reminder markers (any accidental extra disk is a spare, not additional Presence for play), a different Spirit panel, and that Spirit's four Unique cards as their starting hand. Each starts on a different Island Board and follows the back-of-panel setup exactly. Where several choices equally satisfy setup, choose freely; separate Presence-placement instructions may use the same land. Put remaining disks on the dashed spaces of both Presence tracks; the leftmost solid starting spaces remain uncovered. Starting boards do not restrict where a Spirit can act after setup.
7. **Initial Explore:** Reveal the top Invader card and Explore normally. Then put it face-up in **Build**. This Explore is the last part of setup; Ravage starts empty. The first actual turn begins with the Spirit Phase.

For two, any fitting arrangement is legal; the rulebook illustrates bottom-to-bottom with Oceans facing opposite outer corners. For three use the triangular layout, and for four the two-row parallelogram layout illustrated in CORE pp.6–7. [FAQ .7w4g8pg] Populate every land with its printed Invader, Dahan and Blight setup icons. Setup Blight comes from the box, never the Blight pool, and does not cascade or destroy Presence.
2. **Invader deck:** Shuffle each stage separately. Remove one card of each stage unseen. Stack **3 Stage I cards on top, 4 Stage II below them, 5 Stage III at the bottom**. Put this 12-card deck in Explore.
3. **Fear:** Put **4 Fear markers per Spirit** in the Fear Pool. Shuffle the 15 Fear Cards and use 9 unseen: three cards, Terror II divider, three cards, Terror III divider, three cards, from top to bottom. Start at Terror I. Leave space for Earned Fear Cards and Fear discard.
4. **Blight:** Randomly select a Blight Card, Healthy Island side up; do not inspect its reverse. Put **2 Blight per Spirit plus exactly 1 additional Blight total** on it. This is the official initial-pool correction. The additional 1 is applied only at setup, never again on a card flip. Remaining box Blight is separate from this pool.
5. **Supply:** Shuffle Minor and Major decks separately, each with its own discard. Make Invaders, Dahan and Energy available to everyone.
6. **Spirits:** Each player takes one color's 13 Presence and reminder markers (any accidental extra disk is a spare, not additional Presence for play), a different Spirit panel, and that Spirit's four Unique cards as their starting hand. Each starts on a different Island Board and follows the back-of-panel setup exactly. Where several choices equally satisfy setup, choose freely; separate Presence-placement instructions may use the same land. Put remaining disks on the dashed spaces of both Presence tracks; the leftmost solid starting spaces remain uncovered. Starting boards do not restrict where a Spirit can act after setup.
7. **Initial Explore:** Reveal the top Invader card and Explore normally. Then put it face-up in **Build**. This Explore is the last part of setup; Ravage starts empty. The first actual turn begins with the Spirit Phase.

requested_parts: What is the required order of an individual Spirit's Growth, normal track Energy gain, and actual playing/paying for Power Cards?
May the Spirit take its normal Energy income before finishing Growth or actually play/pay before Growth?
If Growth uncovers a higher Energy number, is that number used for normal income in this same Spirit Phase?
answers.answer: Growth → normal Energy → play/pay. Must finish Growth first; newly uncovered Energy number used same phase.

You may instead **reposition any of your island Presence**, even with track disks remaining: first measure range and select the destination using existing Presence, including the disk about to be repositioned, then take a disk from anywhere on the island. This is still an Add Presence instruction, not a Move instruction. Destroyed Presence cannot be used unless explicitly permitted.
- **Move Presence:** A curved movement arrow moves the specified Presence from its present location up to the shown distance; this differs from Add/reposition. Push/Gather Presence uses normal adjacency rules. Instructions are mandatory where possible; a move up to a Range can be zero.
- **Gain Energy:** Gain the displayed amount in addition to normal income.
- **Gain a Power Card:** Use the Actions procedure below.
- **Reclaim:** Return all cards in your personal discard to hand, not cards currently in play or forgotten cards.

- The **targeting Range box** gives the maximum land distance from **one of your Presence**. Range 0 requires your Presence in the target land. Origin icons may require your Sacred Site or Presence in a particular terrain.

- Resolve instructions in printed order, doing as much as possible. Inability to perform one instruction does not prohibit playing or using a Power on an otherwise legal target. Target restrictions are in its target bar, not implied by its text. You may even target a land where the effects accomplish nothing, but must actually attempt the text to count as using/targeting the Power.
- You may forego the whole Power, but cannot arbitrarily omit a possible mandatory instruction after starting. “Up to” allows zero. “Or” chooses between its adjoining clauses, not other separate text on the card. Choose the branch **before resolving either option**; you cannot start one to inspect its results and then switch to the other. [FAQ .9v5kcmx]

Apply the **Power user's** Range bonuses, even if another Spirit supplies the measurement origin. **Blazing Renewal** explicitly uses the Power user's Presence as its origin. Bonuses belonging only to the instructed Spirit do not extend someone else's Power. At any time, trade stored Invaders: **X printed Health worth of drowned Invaders for 1 Energy**, X = number of Spirits; ignore Health modifiers and make change. They need not be exchanged when Drowned; Ocean may exchange them between actions during a later Spirit Phase, including before paying for cards. Dahan drowning gives no Energy. Ordinary destruction, including thematically watery Powers, is not Drowning unless specified. Humans cannot stay there between action trees: if Drowning fails, Push survivors to non-Ocean lands within that action. This is an actual Push and can trigger applicable movement effects, unlike later cleanup. Failed Drowning yields no Energy. Remaining illegal humans are cleaned up to the nearest legal land afterward. Cleanup is not an action, move, removal or destruction and triggers nothing, and occurs before the outcome check. If no legal land exists return humans to supply as cleanup. [Core: .7w4g8qy, .9v5kbka, .7w4g8pb, .9v5ka9g, .7w4g8r4, .9v5kfqb, .9v5kfqs, .7w4gdtl]

An explicit instruction to Damage or Destroy Dahan does nothing to those Dahan; skip that instruction and resolve the rest of the Power normally. For each Power use, evaluate what it would destroy if resolved normally: generate **0 Fear per Explorer, 2 per Town, 5 per City**, and Push the would-be-destroyed Explorers/Towns. No real Damage is marked, so different Powers or a Repeat cannot combine their hypothetical Damage; multiple instructions **within one Power** can. Existing real Damage from others helps its hypothetical destruction and remains unchanged afterward. Within a single Power use, a given Invader can be pretend-destroyed only once. Repeats can “destroy” the same piece again for Fear. It does not get bonuses conditional on **actual** destruction (e.g., Mists of Oblivion or Vengeance of the Dead) from these pretend destructions. [Core: .7w4g7yx, .7w4g7yu, .7w4g8pj, .9v5kfh3, .9v5katc, .bu6oc6g]
- **Bringer's exceptions:** Fear Cards and Dahan counterattacks after its Defend deal real Damage, because they are not its Power's Damage. Reducing Health or replacing a damaged piece with a lower-Health one can cause real destruction by core Health rules. If Bringer Pushes a “destroyed” Town into Ocean, Ocean's separate Drowning destroys it: **3 total Fear** (2 from Bringer, 1 from Ocean). **Spirits May Yet Dream** can flip any Fear Card, earned or anywhere in the deck. Its Element-granting level gives the target Spirit one Element of a type it already has at least one of; it cannot grant a currently absent Element type. [Core: .9v5ka92, .7w4g9jv, .9v5kf34, can-bringer-destroy-things-indirectly, .7w4g8pf, .7w4g8rd]
- **Call on Midnight's Dream:** “Forget this Power” refers to that card, not the newly gained card. Forgetting it to satisfy the gained Major's ordinary Forget requirement also satisfies its conditional; no second Forget is required. The forgotten card leaves play and cannot later be repeated via the normal once-this-turn permission. [Core: .9v5kc3z, .7w4gani, .9v5ka8w]

requested_parts: Dread Apparitions has already resolved in a land. A normal Spirit Power there generates 1 printed Fear and destroys one Town, generating another 1 Fear. Which of those Fear sources count for Dread Apparitions, and counting only this later Power’s Fear, how much additional Defend does it add?
Separately, Bringer’s Power there generates exactly 2 Fear from To Dream a Thousand Deaths pretend-destroying a Town and no other Fear. Does that Fear count, and how much additional Defend is added?
answers.answer: Dread Apparitions adds Defend only for Power-generated Fear: printed Fear 1 counts, destruction Town Fear doesn't; +1 Defend. Bringer's 2 Fear from To Dream counts; +2 Defend.

requested_parts: Wrap in Wings of Sunlight meets its threshold. Its target land initially has no Dahan, but Dahan are available in adjacent lands. Does its threshold’s “First, Gather up to 3 Dahan” happen before the base Move, so those Dahan can then be moved and the destination Defended, or must the base Move finish first because it is printed higher?
Likewise, with Dissolve the Bonds of Kinship’s threshold, does its Invader-on-Invader Damage happen before or after Pushing the Explorers?
answers.answer: Threshold “First” executes before base, gather then move/defend. Dissolve threshold damage before Explorer Push.

requested_parts: List the five phases of an ordinary turn in order. If one Spirit has finished playing and paying while another is still choosing Growth, may the first begin resolving a Fast Power?
Within the Fast Power Phase, must Powers follow player order, or may players choose their sequence?

evidence.text: Each turn follows **Spirit Phase → Fast Power Phase → Invader Phase → Slow Power Phase → Time Passes**. Finish a phase before beginning the next. Players choose the order of Powers within the appropriate Power Phase, completing one before the next. All players act simultaneously within a phase and may discuss freely. requested_parts: After a Spirit has followed its back-panel island setup, where are its remaining Presence disks put?
Are the leftmost solid-circle Energy and Card Plays numbers covered?
answers.answer: Remaining Presence disks placed on dashed spaces of both tracks; leftmost solid starting spaces uncovered.

evidence.text:
1. **Island:** Randomly choose one Island Board per Spirit and join the balanced sides into the island. For one Spirit use one board. For two, any fitting arrangement is legal; the rulebook illustrates bottom-to-bottom with Oceans facing opposite outer corners. For three use the triangular layout, and for four the two-row parallelogram layout illustrated in CORE pp.6–7. [FAQ .7w4g8pg] Populate every land with its printed Invader, Dahan and Blight setup icons. Setup Blight comes from the box, never the Blight pool, and does not cascade or destroy Presence.
2. **Invader deck:** Shuffle each stage separately. Remove one card of each stage unseen. Stack **3 Stage I cards on top, 4 Stage II below them, 5 Stage III at the bottom**. Put this 12-card deck in Explore.
3. **Fear:** Put **4 Fear markers per Spirit** in the Fear Pool. Shuffle the 15 Fear Cards and use 9 unseen: three cards, Terror II divider, three cards, Terror III divider, three cards, from top to bottom. Start at Terror I. Leave space for Earned Fear Cards and Fear discard.
4. **Blight:** Randomly select a Blight Card, Healthy Island side up; do not inspect its reverse. Put **2 Blight per Spirit plus exactly 1 additional Blight total** on it. This is the official initial-pool correction. The additional 1 is applied only at setup, never again on a card flip. Remaining box Blight is separate from this pool.
5. **Supply:** Shuffle Minor and Major decks separately, each with its own discard. Make Invaders, Dahan and Energy available to everyone.
6. **Spirits:** Each player takes one color's 13 Presence and reminder markers (any accidental extra disk is a spare, not additional Presence for play), a different Spirit panel, and that Spirit's four Unique cards as their starting hand. Each starts on a different Island Board and follows the back-of-panel setup exactly. Where several choices equally satisfy setup, choose freely; separate Presence-placement instructions may use the same land. Put remaining disks on the dashed spaces of both Presence tracks; the leftmost solid starting spaces remain uncovered. Starting boards do not restrict where a Spirit can act after setup.
7. **Initial Explore:** Reveal the top Invader card and Explore normally. Then put it face-up in **Build**. This Explore is the last part of setup; Ravage starts empty. The first actual turn begins with the Spirit Phase.

Island-wide effects defined for a class of lands check current contents when relevant (for example, **Dahan on their Guard** counts Dahan when Damage occurs). **Encompassing Ward** follows the target Spirit's current Presence, rather than marking the lands occupied when it was used. requested_parts: When using a beginner Spirit’s Power Progression, what must be done during setup with the Minor and Major cards listed on that Progression?
Should they stay in the shared shuffled decks to be drawn normally by other gains?
answers.answer: Remove listed Minor/Major from shared decks and reserve; not available for ordinary gains.

evidence.text:
1. **Island:** Randomly choose one Island Board per Spirit and join the balanced sides into the island. For one Spirit use one board. For two, any fitting arrangement is legal; the rulebook illustrates bottom-to-bottom with Oceans facing opposite outer corners. For three use the triangular layout, and for four the two-row parallelogram layout illustrated in CORE pp.6–7. [FAQ .7w4g8pg] Populate every land with its printed Invader, Dahan and Blight setup icons. Setup Blight comes from the box, never the Blight pool, and does not cascade or destroy Presence.
2. **Invader deck:** Shuffle each stage separately. Remove one card of each stage unseen. Stack **3 Stage I cards on top, 4 Stage II below them, 5 Stage III at the bottom**. Put this 12-card deck in Explore.
3. **Fear:** Put **4 Fear markers per Spirit** in the Fear Pool. Shuffle the 15 Fear Cards and use 9 unseen: three cards, Terror II divider, three cards, Terror III divider, three cards, from top to bottom. Start at Terror I. Leave space for Earned Fear Cards and Fear discard.
4. **Blight:** Randomly select a Blight Card, Healthy Island side up; do not inspect its reverse. Put **2 Blight per Spirit plus exactly 1 additional Blight total** on it. This is the official initial-pool correction. The additional 1 is applied only at setup, never again on a card flip. Remaining box Blight is separate from this pool.
5. **Supply:** Shuffle Minor and Major decks separately, each with its own discard. Make Invaders, Dahan and Energy available to everyone.
6. **Spirits:** Each player takes one color's 13 Presence and reminder markers (any accidental extra disk is a spare, not additional Presence for play), a different Spirit panel, and that Spirit's four Unique cards as their starting hand. Each starts on a different Island Board and follows the back-of-panel setup exactly. Where several choices equally satisfy setup, choose freely; separate Presence-placement instructions may use the same land. Put remaining disks on the dashed spaces of both Presence tracks; the leftmost solid starting spaces remain uncovered. Starting boards do not restrict where a Spirit can act after setup.
7. **Initial Explore:** Reveal the top Invader card and Explore normally. Then put it face-up in **Build**. This Explore is the last part of setup; Ravage starts empty. The first actual turn begins with the Spirit Phase.

**Introductory alternatives (CORE p.3):** Choose a low-complexity Spirit: Lightning's Swift Strike, Vital Strength of the Earth, River Surges in Sunlight, or Shadows Flicker Like Flame. A new player may use its Power Progression: remove the listed Minor and Major cards from the shared decks and reserve them; on gaining a Power, take the next one into hand instead of drawing four. Gaining a Major still requires Forgetting a card. If everyone is new, omit the Blight Card and use the printed board pool: **5 Blight per Spirit +1 total** at setup, losing if it empties; there is no flip or ongoing Blighted effect. Do not use an Adversary or Scenario. Progressions are a teaching aid, not compulsory for low-complexity Spirits.

requested_parts: Do the normal cascade and one-Presence-per-Spirit destruction rules apply to Blight placed during setup, or only to Blight added after setup?
answers.answer: Setup Blight doesn't cascade or destroy Presence. Applies only added after setup.

For two, any fitting arrangement is legal; the rulebook illustrates bottom-to-bottom with Oceans facing opposite outer corners. For three use the triangular layout, and for four the two-row parallelogram layout illustrated in CORE pp.6–7. 2. **Invader deck:** Shuffle each stage separately. Remove one card of each stage unseen. Stack **3 Stage I cards on top, 4 Stage II below them, 5 Stage III at the bottom**. Put this 12-card deck in Explore.
3. **Fear:** Put **4 Fear markers per Spirit** in the Fear Pool. Shuffle the 15 Fear Cards and use 9 unseen: three cards, Terror II divider, three cards, Terror III divider, three cards, from top to bottom. Start at Terror I. Leave space for Earned Fear Cards and Fear discard.

This is the official initial-pool correction. The additional 1 is applied only at setup, never again on a card flip. Remaining box Blight is separate from this pool.
5. **Supply:** Shuffle Minor and Major decks separately, each with its own discard. Make Invaders, Dahan and Energy available to everyone.
6. **Spirits:** Each player takes one color's 13 Presence and reminder markers (any accidental extra disk is a spare, not additional Presence for play), a different Spirit panel, and that Spirit's four Unique cards as their starting hand. Each starts on a different Island Board and follows the back-of-panel setup exactly. Where several choices equally satisfy setup, choose freely; separate Presence-placement instructions may use the same land. Put remaining disks on the dashed spaces of both Presence tracks; the leftmost solid starting spaces remain uncovered. Starting boards do not restrict where a Spirit can act after setup.

requested_parts: In the first ordinary turn after standard setup, the Ravage Action Space has no Invader Card. Do Invaders Ravage anyway or draw a card for Ravage, or is that action omitted?
What is the general rule for an empty Invader Action Space?
answers.answer: No Ravage, no draw. Empty action space does nothing.

This is an actual Push and can trigger applicable movement effects, unlike later cleanup. Failed Drowning yields no Energy. - **Bringer's exceptions:** Fear Cards and Dahan counterattacks after its Defend deal real Damage, because they are not its Power's Damage. Its Element-granting level gives the target Spirit one Element of a type it already has at least one of; it cannot grant a currently absent Element type. [Core: .9v5ka92, .7w4g9jv, .9v5kf34, can-bringer-destroy-things-indirectly, .7w4g8pf, .7w4g8rd]
- **Call on Midnight's Dream:** “Forget this Power” refers to that card, not the newly gained card. Forgetting it to satisfy the gained Major's ordinary Forget requirement also satisfies its conditional; no second Forget is required. The forgotten card leaves play and cannot later be repeated via the normal once-this-turn permission. [Core: .9v5kc3z, .7w4gani, .9v5ka8w]

requested_parts: Three Fear Cards were earned in a known order. During the Fear step, may players inspect all three before resolving the first?
In which order are they resolved, and where does each card go once resolved?
answers.answer: No lookahead; resolve earned order, one at a time, discard each to Fear discard after resolution.

evidence.text:
1. **Blighted Island:** If the Blight Card is Blighted, follow its instructions at the specified timing (typically start of each Invader Phase). No such step applies with the printed no-card pool.
2. **Fear:** Turn the earned face-down stack over and resolve its cards **in the order earned**, one at a time, without looking ahead. Use **only the current Terror Level's effect**, even if the card was earned at a lower level. Discard each resolved card to Fear discard. Fear earned during this step can earn more cards: append them to the bottom of the resolving stack and resolve them this same step. Subsequent cards use any newly reached Terror Level. Fear earned later, such as in Ravage or Slow, waits for the next Fear step.
3. **Ravage:** Resolve the card in Ravage, if any.
4. **Build:** Resolve the card in Build, if any.
5. **Explore:** Reveal the next Invader card and resolve Explore. If a card must be drawn and the deck is empty, lose. Revealing the last existing card is not itself a loss.
6. **Advance cards:** Discard the old Ravage card; slide Build to Ravage and the just-revealed Explore card to Build.

requested_parts: A normal Power deals 3 Damage in a land with a healthy Town and City. Must players finish destroying one chosen Invader before assigning Damage to the other, or may they assign 1 to the Town and 2 to the City so both survive?
answers.answer: Damage can be distributed however desired; may assign 1 Town and 2 City, both survive.

requested_parts: An instruction explicitly downgrades two Invaders simultaneously. May one City be selected twice, first becoming a Town and then an Explorer, or must the pieces be selected before either replacement?
Contrast two separate players’ legal Trade Suffers III actions.
answers.answer: Select all before simultaneous replacement; one City can't downgrade twice in same instruction. Separate completed actions/players may replace resulting Town again.

- The **targeting Range box** gives the maximum land distance from **one of your Presence**. Range 0 requires your Presence in the target land. Origin icons may require your Sacred Site or Presence in a particular terrain.
- Target restrictions may specify terrain, Coastal/Inland, contents, or a Spirit. A slash between piece/terrain icons means either or both types, not an additional allowance for each.
- Unless explicitly different, use **one target land or Spirit, once per turn**. Multiple effects and all innate levels apply to that same target. You cannot pay twice for an ordinary card use or use an innate twice just by having twice its Elements.
- Resolve instructions in printed order, doing as much as possible. Inability to perform one instruction does not prohibit playing or using a Power on an otherwise legal target. Target restrictions are in its target bar, not implied by its text. You may even target a land where the effects accomplish nothing, but must actually attempt the text to count as using/targeting the Power.
- You may forego the whole Power, but cannot arbitrarily omit a possible mandatory instruction after starting. “Up to” allows zero. “Or” chooses between its adjoining clauses, not other separate text on the card. Choose the branch **before resolving either option**; you cannot start one to inspect its results and then switch to the other. [FAQ .9v5kcmx]
- Resolve the base effect and every met threshold in printed order **unless explicit timing text says otherwise**: “First” and “Before” can place a threshold instruction ahead of earlier-printed base instructions. A level saying **Instead** replaces previous effects rather than adding to them. You may treat yourself as having fewer Elements **for the whole Power**, consistently, rather than selecting individual thresholds to omit.

Apply a threshold changing Speed, Range or targeting when checking that attribute, before the ordinary effects: for example, Thunderspeaker's met Fast threshold permits using its Innate in Fast. Speed/Range/targeting modifiers are checked in time to use them before targeting, and an “or” choice is made before its branch resolves.
- Non-board-changing effects last for this turn only unless explicitly stated otherwise. Defend and action skips do not remain for future turns.

**Destroy** returns pieces to supply regardless of Health when directly instructed. Every destroyed Town generates **1 Fear** and every destroyed City **2 Fear**, in addition to explicit Fear from the effect. Explorers generate none automatically. **Remove** returns the specified pieces without requiring Damage to reach their Health and without destruction Fear. **Replace** removes a piece and adds another, retaining its marked Damage: the replacement itself produces no Fear, but if the retained Damage destroys the new piece, destruction Fear applies normally. For simultaneous replacements, select all pieces before replacing any: the same original City cannot become a Town and then an Explorer within that one simultaneous instruction. Separate completed instructions or actions may replace the resulting piece again (e.g., successive players resolving **Trade Suffers** at Terror III).

Fear from **To Dream a Thousand Deaths** counts; normal Fear for destroying Towns/Cities does not, even when a Power caused the destruction. [Original core card text]

It grants no Defend if zero Dahan move: there is no moved-to land. Moving Dahan to their original land can count as Move if the Power permits. **Blazing Renewal** permits its target Spirit to add its destroyed Presence directly to one legal island land, not to tracks. Its printed “adds 2” is mandatory to the extent possible, using the Power user's Presence for its internal Range; it cannot deal threshold Damage with no destroyed Presence restored: “that land” refers to where it adds Presence. **The Trees and Stones Speak of War** deals 1 Damage per Dahan and grants Defend 2 per Dahan in its target land. Its threshold moves Defend 2 with each Dahan it Pushes, leaving the remaining Defend in the target. Only this Power's Defend 2 per pushed Dahan travels; separate Defend from another effect, such as Words of Warning, stays in its original land. A later Power moving those Dahan does not carry that Defend. [Core: .9v5kfqd, .9v5kfr0, .bu6oc8n, .bu6ocxq]

River's special Wetland-site rule remains River's own. For its base card gains, the **target Spirit** first makes the normal draw-four/keep-one gain; the **using Spirit** then gains one of those same three unkept cards, without drawing another four. In solo, both gains come from that single four-card draw. The threshold also lets the using and target Spirits each independently gift the other one Power Card **from hand**, optionally; cards in play or personal discard cannot be gifted by it. Tidal Boon's “if Dahan are pushed” clause applies only to that Power's own Push. [Core: .9v5kehe, when-does-swiftness-of-lightning-happen, if-a-special-rule-cares-about-elements-when-does-it-check-your-element-total, .7w4gefg]

- **Shadows Flicker Like Flame:** Pay **Shadows of the Dahan**'s 1 Energy when using the Power, to ignore numeric Range to a land with Dahan. For **Darkness Swallows the Unwary**, choosing lower Elements cannot select the second level without the first when both require the same Elements; if destroying Explorers under that level, first Gather an Explorer if able. [Core: .7w4g8pt, .7w4g8nq, .7w4g8r6, .bu6od0c]
- **A Spread of Rampant Green:** **Choke the Land with Green** is optional (some printings omit “may”). When adding Presence via Growth, Green may use destroyed disks instead of track disks even while disks remain on tracks: this is free while Healthy, or costs 1 Energy per destroyed disk while Blighted. This permission applies only to Growth; an ordinary Power needs its own explicit destroyed-Presence permission. Green's separate **Always** Range-2 Jungle/Wetland placement is additional to its one chosen Growth group, including when it chooses Reclaim/gain a Power. It still chooses only one of the optional groups. Growth instructions from multiple options can be ordered together, so a gained Power may inform the mandatory placement. Its explicit regeneration can use destroyed Presence; ordinary placement cannot. [Core: .9v5kc2v, .7w4g8r1, .bu6oegz, .7w4g8nv]

Powers and Special Rules can measure Range through it as a land. [Core: range-through-ocean] Powers can target it and move Invaders/Dahan into it; Blight can cascade into it. Other Spirits' Presence may end up there via a legal Power, including Thunderspeaker accompanying moved Dahan. You can measure Growth placement Range **from existing Ocean Presence**, although normal Growth cannot add to the Ocean just by treating it as a Coastal Wetland. The Growth group explicitly adding two Presence in **any Ocean** can place them in any board's Ocean, even a board where Ocean has no Presence, without a numeric Range requirement. Its other group's Range-1 **Coastal land** placement does not permit placing in the Ocean. Other placement must respect Ocean's land-type restriction unless expressly ignored (e.g., **Indomitable Claim** for Inland Presence). [Core: .bu6odcf, .7w4gef8, .9v5kf36, .9v5ka9o, .9v5kc4i, When-OHG-is-in-play-can-other-pieces-end-up-in-the-Ocean]
- **Drowning:** Ocean's rule Drowns Invaders/Dahan **after** they move into the Ocean on a board with Ocean's Presence; Ocean need not have a disk in the Ocean itself. Drown destroys: Town/City Fear happens immediately, and drowned Invaders go on Ocean's panel. At any time, trade stored Invaders: **X printed Health worth of drowned Invaders for 1 Energy**, X = number of Spirits; ignore Health modifiers and make change. They need not be exchanged when Drowned; Ocean may exchange them between actions during a later Spirit Phase, including before paying for cards. Dahan drowning gives no Energy. Ordinary destruction, including thematically watery Powers, is not Drowning unless specified. If Ocean loses all Presence on that board mid-action, Ocean In Play lasts through the action tree; afterward non-human pieces left there remain physically but out of play until it returns. Humans cannot stay there between action trees: if Drowning fails, Push survivors to non-Ocean lands within that action. This is an actual Push and can trigger applicable movement effects, unlike later cleanup. Failed Drowning yields no Energy. Remaining illegal humans are cleaned up to the nearest legal land afterward. Cleanup is not an action, move, removal or destruction and triggers nothing, and occurs before the outcome check. If no legal land exists return humans to supply as cleanup. [Core: .7w4g8qy, .9v5kbka, .7w4g8pb, .9v5ka9g, .7w4g8r4, .9v5kfqb, .9v5kfqs, .7w4gdtl]
- **Bringer of Dreams and Nightmares:** Its Powers' explicit Damage/Destroy cannot actually harm Invaders/Dahan or destroy anything except its own Presence. An explicit instruction to Damage or Destroy Dahan does nothing to those Dahan; skip that instruction and resolve the rest of the Power normally. For each Power use, evaluate what it would destroy if resolved normally: generate **0 Fear per Explorer, 2 per Town, 5 per City**, and Push the would-be-destroyed Explorers/Towns. No real Damage is marked, so different Powers or a Repeat cannot combine their hypothetical Damage; multiple instructions **within one Power** can. Existing real Damage from others helps its hypothetical destruction and remains unchanged afterward. Within a single Power use, a given Invader can be pretend-destroyed only once. Repeats can “destroy” the same piece again for Fear. It does not get bonuses conditional on **actual** destruction (e.g., Mists of Oblivion or Vengeance of the Dead) from these pretend destructions. [Core: .7w4g7yx, .7w4g7yu, .7w4g8pj, .9v5kfh3, .9v5katc, .bu6oc6g]
- **Bringer's exceptions:** Fear Cards and Dahan counterattacks after its Defend deal real Damage, because they are not its Power's Damage. Bringer can Remove/Replace, add real Blight (destroying Presence normally), modify Invader actions or cause actual Ravage. Reducing Health or replacing a damaged piece with a lower-Health one can cause real destruction by core Health rules. If Bringer Pushes a “destroyed” Town into Ocean, Ocean's separate Drowning destroys it: **3 total Fear** (2 from Bringer, 1 from Ocean). **Spirits May Yet Dream** can flip any Fear Card, earned or anywhere in the deck. Its Element-granting level gives the target Spirit one Element of a type it already has at least one of; it cannot grant a currently absent Element type. [Core: .9v5ka92, .7w4g9jv, .9v5kf34, can-bringer-destroy-things-indirectly, .7w4g8pf, .7w4g8rd]
- **Call on Midnight's Dream:** “Forget this Power” refers to that card, not the newly gained card. Forgetting it to satisfy the gained Major's ordinary Forget requirement also satisfies its conditional; no second Forget is required. The forgotten card leaves play and cannot later be repeated via the normal once-this-turn permission. [Core: .9v5kc3z, .7w4gani, .9v5ka8w]

requested_parts: Assume two Ravage Cards will be resolved in sequence. A land matching the second card is empty when the Ravage step begins, but a triggered effect during the first card moves an Invader there before the second card begins. Does that land Ravage from the second card, or was eligibility locked for the whole step?
answers.answer: Eligibility redetermined for each card; second card includes land if occupied when its eligibility determined.

evidence.text:
1. **Blighted Island:** If the Blight Card is Blighted, follow its instructions at the specified timing (typically start of each Invader Phase). No such step applies with the printed no-card pool.
2. **Fear:** Turn the earned face-down stack over and resolve its cards **in the order earned**, one at a time, without looking ahead. Use **only the current Terror Level's effect**, even if the card was earned at a lower level. Discard each resolved card to Fear discard. Fear earned during this step can earn more cards: append them to the bottom of the resolving stack and resolve them this same step. Subsequent cards use any newly reached Terror Level. Fear earned later, such as in Ravage or Slow, waits for the next Fear step.
3. **Ravage:** Resolve the card in Ravage, if any.
4. **Build:** Resolve the card in Build, if any.
5. **Explore:** Reveal the next Invader card and resolve Explore. If a card must be drawn and the deck is empty, lose. Revealing the last existing card is not itself a loss.
6. **Advance cards:** Discard the old Ravage card; slide Build to Ravage and the just-revealed Explore card to Build.

Before resolving the actions from a card, determine which lands qualify; players choose the order of those lands. Changes during the card do not add newly eligible lands to that list. Determine eligibility anew for each later card, so a land newly occupied during an earlier Ravage card can Ravage under a later matching Ravage card. In a land already due to Ravage, newly arrived Invaders participate when its Ravage resolves. Resolve each land fully, including cascades and triggered effects, and check outcomes before proceeding to the next. [CORE pp.9–10; FAQ pieces-added-or-moved-by-ravages-do-not-cause-more-ravages; .9v5kaam]
